fields.value: Meridian Specialty Insurance (LiftLane rideshare policy, driver was en route to a pickup). No-fault through Harborline Casualty Company.

fields.name: Case Summary
fields.value: Pedestrian struck in the crosswalk by a LiftLane driver turning left. Right tibial plateau fracture with ORIF, concussion with post-concussive headaches.

fields.name: Policy Limits
fields.value:
Defendant liability: $1,000,000 per incident (rideshare period 2, en route to pickup)
No-fault: $50,000

fields.name: Liability Assessment
fields.value: Strong on the client's account, but the police report places her outside the crosswalk.

notes.subject: Intake: pedestrian knockdown
notes.detail: Lucia Ferreyra, 31, pharmacy technician. On {{-640}} around 7:40 pm she was crossing the Grand Concourse at East 183rd Street in the crosswalk with the walk signal when a Toyota driven by Owen Tallis turned left and hit her. She says she was halfway across and the walk sign was still white. Tallis was driving for LiftLane and had the app on, heading to pick up a rider. Admitted to Concourse General with a right tibial plateau fracture and a concussion.

notes.subject: Police report reviewed: problem
notes.detail: MV-104 is in. The officer's narrative says the pedestrian was crossing approximately 20 feet north of the crosswalk against the signal, based on the driver's account. This contradicts what Lucia told us and what she wrote in her signed statement. No independent witness is listed. Need to look for video from the bodega on the corner and the bus camera.

notes.subject: Video canvass
notes.detail: Investigator canvassed the corner. The bodega camera faces the wrong way. The MTA bus that was stopped at 183rd Street may have a forward camera; preservation request sent to MTA.

notes.subject: Settlement demand served
notes.detail: Served the settlement demand on Meridian Specialty Insurance for $650,000 with records, bills, the surgical report and the neurology narrative.

notes.subject: First offer
notes.detail: Meridian adjuster offered $85,000, citing the police report placing Lucia outside the crosswalk and arguing comparative fault of at least 50 percent.

notes.subject: Counteroffer
notes.detail: Countered at $475,000. Pointed out that the driver's account is the only basis for the officer's narrative and that the tibial plateau fracture required surgery and hardware.

notes.subject: Second offer
notes.detail: Meridian raised the offer to $140,000. Adjuster says the MTA bus video does not exist. We have not confirmed that ourselves. Need Lucia's authority before the mediation.

notes.subject: Medicaid lien
notes.detail: Medicaid asserts $18,640.00. Must get a final lien letter and request a reduction for procurement costs before any settlement is disbursed. Harborline no-fault paid the basic economic loss.

emails.subject: Coverage confirmation
emails.body: Our records show the LiftLane driver app was active and the driver was en route to a passenger pickup at the time of the incident. The applicable limit is $1,000,000 per incident. Arturo Delmas, Claims Examiner.

emails.subject: Offer: Ferreyra v. Tallis
emails.body: After review of the demand package, Meridian offers $85,000.00 to resolve all claims. The police report places your client outside the crosswalk and crossing against the signal. Arturo Delmas.

emails.subject: Revised offer
emails.body: Meridian is prepared to increase its offer to $140,000.00. The MTA has advised that no forward camera footage was retained for that bus. Arturo Delmas.

emails.subject: Mediation date
emails.body: Confirming mediation before the Hon. Clara Whitcomb (Ret.) at Midtown Resolution Center. Please send your mediation statement one week ahead.

emails.subject: Medicaid lien notice
emails.from: New York State Department of Health, Medicaid
emails.body: This office asserts a lien of $18,640.00 for medical assistance provided to Lucia Ferreyra related to the incident of {{-640}}. Do not disburse settlement funds without written lien resolution.

calls.subject: Client call: first offer
calls.body: Told Lucia about the $85,000 offer. She was upset that they are calling her a jaywalker. She repeated that she was in the crosswalk with the walk sign.

calls.subject: Client call: second offer
calls.body: Told Lucia the offer is now $140,000. She wants to think about it and talk with her husband before giving us a number. No authority yet.

tasks.name: By client: Lucia Ferreyra - Settlement authority before mediation

tasks.description: Due one week before the mediation.

tasks.name: Confirm with the MTA directly whether bus camera footage exists
tasks.description: Meridian says no footage was retained. Verify ourselves.

tasks.name: Final Medicaid lien letter and reduction request

pages.text:
POLICE ACCIDENT REPORT MV-104AN
Precinct: 046   Date of accident: {{iso:-640}}   Time: 19:42
Location: Grand Concourse at E 183 St, Bronx
Vehicle 1: Toyota Camry, operator Owen Tallis
Pedestrian: Lucia Ferreyra, age 31, injured, removed to Concourse General Hospital

Accident description / officer's notes: Per operator of Vehicle 1, V1 was making a left turn from Grand Concourse onto E 183 St on a green signal when pedestrian entered roadway approx 20 ft north of crosswalk against the signal and was struck by front of V1. Pedestrian was not interviewed at scene due to injuries. No independent witnesses located.

Apparent contributing factors: Pedestrian error/confusion (V1 per operator).

STATEMENT OF LUCIA FERREYRA
Given at the office of counsel on {{iso:-625}}.

On the evening of {{iso:-640}} I was walking home from work. I waited at the corner of the Grand Concourse and East 183rd Street until the walk sign came on. I started across inside the white lines of the crosswalk. When I was about halfway across, a gray Toyota turning left came toward me fast and hit my right leg. I did not see it slow down. The walk sign was still white when I was hit.

I have read this statement and it is true.
Signed: Lucia Ferreyra
